DOES CONSENSUS PRICE IN THE IAS 29 NET MONETARY GAIN/(LOSS)? No evidence that it does separately. Q2 2026 earnings call (2026-07-28; Motley Fool transcript https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/07/29/unilever-ul-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/): the only analyst reference to hyperinflation is David Hayes (Jefferies): "Pricing was obviously flat in the quarter despite the hyperinflation or contributions in the region. So clearly, some sort of price reset going on there..." This is a question about pricing and underlying sales growth, not about the monetary line. CEO Fernando Fernandez framed Argentina only as a volume story: "In the second quarter, Argentina delivered high single-digit volume growth..." The transcript never mentions net monetary gains/losses, IAS 29, or Türkiye. This matches the earlier live research recorded in valuation_inputs.json's consensus.note (Q1 + Q2 2026 transcripts, TipRanks/MarketScreener/MarketBeat commentary): analysts treat Argentina/Türkiye as volume/pricing stories plus a generic aggregate currency headwind. In public material, no one separates the net monetary gain/(loss) from FX translation. Limitation: paywalled broker notes (e.g. Jefferies, Deutsche Bank, Barclays, Bernstein, JP Morgan, UBS) were not accessible, so this conclusion rests on public transcripts and aggregators only.
